items.title: The 1931 Yangtze flood killed millions
items.claim: What was the death toll of the 1931 China floods?

options.text: Around 100,000 — comparable to other major river floods
Estimates range from 422,000 to over 4 million dead — likely the deadliest natural disaster of the 20th century

items.reveal:
The 1931 floods affected the Yangtze, Huai and Yellow river basins after extreme monsoon rainfall. Chris Courtney's 'The Nature of Disaster in China' (2018) places direct deaths from drowning at around 150,000 and total deaths including disease and famine at perhaps 2 million; older estimates went higher.

Wuhan was submerged for weeks. The Republic of China government's response was overwhelmed by the simultaneous Mukden Incident (September 1931, Japanese invasion of Manchuria).
items.why: River flooding remains the deadliest natural hazard category by long-term death toll. Vulnerability is not just about hazard — it's about state capacity, infrastructure and political moment.

items.title: The 1931 China floods may be the deadliest natural disaster in recorded history
items.claim: What was the death toll of the 1931 China floods?

options.text: Estimates range from 422,000 to over 4 million dead — counting drowning, disease and famine after extreme monsoon rainfall on the Yangtze, Huai and Yellow river basins; likely the deadliest natural disaster of the 20th century

items.reveal:
The 1931 floods affected the Yangtze, Huai and Yellow river basins after exceptional monsoon rainfall. Chris Courtney's 'The Nature of Disaster in China' (2018) gives careful estimates: direct deaths from drowning around 150,000; deaths including subsequent disease and famine around 2 million.

Wuhan was submerged for weeks. The Republic of China government — distracted by the Japanese invasion of Manchuria the same September — was overwhelmed. Nanjing's Yangtze flood mark of 1931 is still visible.

The Three Gorges Dam (completed 2006) is partly justified as flood control; the 1931, 1954 and 1998 Yangtze floods all killed thousands.
items.why: River flooding remains the deadliest natural hazard category by long-term death toll. Vulnerability is not just hazard — it is state capacity, infrastructure and timing of other crises.

items.title: Most workers in low-income countries are in the informal economy
items.claim: What share of employment is informal in LICs?

options.text: Around 90% of employment in low-income countries and around 60% globally is informal (ILO, 2018) — without formal contracts, social protection or tax registration

items.reveal:
The International Labour Organization defines informal employment as work without legal recognition or social protection. The estimate is around 2 billion workers globally, with concentrations in sub-Saharan Africa (around 89% of non-agricultural employment) and South Asia (around 86%).

Key activities: street vending, waste picking, domestic work, small-scale agriculture. Many informal workers are women.

The term came from Keith Hart's 1971 fieldwork in Accra, Ghana. The ILO has worked since 2015 (Recommendation 204) on transitioning workers to the formal economy.
items.why: Models of 'employment' built on the Global North get developing-world economies wrong. The informal sector is not marginal — it is the modal experience of work for billions.
